newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fund selling knocks Singapore shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Fund selling knocks Singapore shares at close.

text.p: A wave of across-the-board selling by some foreign funds pushed the Singapore stock market down sharply just before the close on Tuesday.
The unweighted benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed down 32.02 points at 2,201.97 on a volume of 538 million shares. It was around 2,215 points a few minutes before trading ended.

Almost all the large STII component stocks lost ground, led by car retailer Cycle & Carriage and diversified maritime group Keppel Corp which lost 40 and 30 cents to Singapore $15.80 and S$10.20 respectively.

Dealers said funds had been encouraged to sell some blue chips by an announcement by Morgan Stanley & Co last week that it would cut the weighting it gave to the foreign tranches of some Singapore companies in one of its indices.
Some were also worried about the prospects for the 1996 financial reporting season, which kicked off this week.
Dealers could not explain the wave of late selling.
Malaysian over-the-counter stocks continued to take much of the volume, with Malaysian shares Promet Berhad and Insas Berhad together trading almost 60 million shares.
